verses.text: Solomon made a marriage agreement with Pharaoh, king of Egypt, by marrying Pharaoh's daughter. He brought her to the City of David until he had finished building his own palace, the LORD's temple, and the wall around Jerusalem.
The people were still offering sacrifices at the high places, the local places of worship, because a temple for the LORD's name had not yet been built.
Solomon loved the LORD and followed the laws of his father David. But he also offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places.
The king went to Gibeon to offer sacrifices, because that was the most important high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
At Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream at night. God said, "Ask for whatever you want me to give you."

Solomon answered, "You showed great and faithful love to your servant, my father David, because he lived before you faithfully, rightly, and with an honest heart. And you have continued to show him this great love by giving him a son to sit on his throne today.
Now, LORD my God, you have made me, your servant, king in place of my father David. But I am like a little child. I don't know how to lead.
Your servant is here among the people you have chosen, a great nation with too many people to count.
So give your servant a heart that understands, so that I can judge your people and know the difference between right and wrong. For who is able to rule this great people of yours?"
The Lord was pleased that Solomon had asked for this.

So God said to him, "You have asked for this. You did not ask for a long life for yourself, or for riches, or for the death of your enemies. Instead you asked for understanding, so that you can judge fairly.
So I will do what you asked. I will give you a wise and understanding heart. There has never been anyone like you before, and there will never be anyone like you again.
I will also give you what you did not ask for: both riches and honour. As long as you live, no other king will be as great as you.
And if you follow my ways and keep my laws and commands, as your father David did, I will give you a long life."

Then Solomon woke up and realised it had been a dream. He went back to Jerusalem and stood in front of the ark of the LORD's covenant. He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and gave a feast for all his officials.
One day two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood in front of him.
One of them said, "Please, my lord, this woman and I live in the same house. I had a baby while she was there with me.
Three days after my baby was born, this woman also had a baby. We were alone. There was no one else in the house except the two of us.
During the night this woman's son died, because she rolled over on top of him.
She got up in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while I, your servant, was asleep. She put him in her arms and put her dead son in my arms.
When I got up in the morning to feed my son, I saw that he was dead. But when I looked at him closely in the morning light, I saw that he was not the son I had given birth to."

The other woman said, "No! The living one is my son, and the dead one is yours." But the first woman said, "No! The dead one is yours, and the living one is mine." And so they argued in front of the king.
Then the king said, "One of you says, 'My son is alive and your son is dead.' The other says, 'No! Your son is dead and mine is alive.'"
Then the king said, "Bring me a sword." So they brought a sword to the king.
The king said, "Cut the living child in two, and give half to one woman and half to the other."

Then the real mother of the living child was filled with love for her son. She said to the king, "Please, my lord, give her the living baby! Don't kill him!" But the other woman said, "He won't be mine or yours. Cut him in two!"
Then the king gave his decision: "Give the living baby to the first woman. Do not kill him. She is his mother."
When all Israel heard about the king's decision, they respected him deeply, because they saw that God had given him wisdom to judge fairly.
